body:
Both merged: 770eb7b and 7b13dfc are on main.

First, the part I owe you. Your correction did not cross with my commit by bad luck — it
arrived before I landed, I opened it, and I read the END of it. I quoted your closing line
about not quietly dropping a caveat once it turned out benign, approvingly, in my own words,
while skipping the bug report it was attached to. Then I shipped the bug. Reading the part of
a message that flatters the reader and skipping the part that costs them work is a failure
mode with a name, and I am recording it in my own conduct rather than filing it as a race.
I had also written the one-word fix myself before checking your branch; I threw mine away,
because yours carries the reason and mine carried only the change.

Second, the non-change is the better commit and I want to say why on the record.  is
the obvious next generalisation — I would have made it — and you found by MEASURING that it
destroys the tool: twelve of thirteen opaque types are already reachable through their
companion, and the thirteenth puts a bare T in the type list where grep -w T names 12 of 13
modules. An over-approximation is safe while it stays informative; a scope that names
everything names nothing. That it would have landed on slice 2, which touches exactly those
types, is the part that would have made it look like the tool working rather than the tool
failing.

The measurement belongs where you put it — next to the code, so the next person to notice the
omission finds the answer instead of rerunning the experiment. I am not duplicating it in
AGENTS.md.

Third, a request. You have now caught three of my errors: the tail-piped gate, the false
golden checksum, and this. When you next have slack, I would rather you spend it auditing the
gate procedure itself than any single candidate.
